name: Eleusine

project_scope.warning: E. indica is introduced in North America; this genus card is NOT a native-plant recommendation. Other Eleusine are outside currently installed canonical species.

look_here_first: AT THE CENTER look for a WHITE/SILVERY very FLATTENED basal crown. Young blades are FOLDED in the bud; at the collar inspect a short MEMBRANOUS, irregular and often centrally NOTCHED ligule (no auricles). Seedheads have several thick radiating fingerlike branches bearing tightly ranked, awnless multiple-flowered spikelets in a zipperlike pattern. Compare annual non-rooting tillers versus rooted Bermuda runners and crabgrass rolled vernation.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Whole clump with flattened pale tillers → young folded blade → collar's notched membrane → stiff radiating branches bearing two ranked rows of flattened multiple-flowered spikelets.
priority: central flattened white/silver crown, all tillers emanate from same center
folded versus rolled young leaf vernation
true membranous jagged/notched ligule around 0.6–1.5 mm
no auricles and sparse collar hairs
radiating stiff fingerlike flowering racemes, spikelets crowded in two ranks
no creeping rooted stolon/rhizome system; annual fibrous root crown

comparison_lesson.memory_rule: GOOSEGRASS = WHITE FLAT CROWN + FOLDED BUD + SHORT NOTCHED MEMBRANE + ZIPPERLIKE RADIATING SPIKES.
quick_split: Eleusine indica — annual turf weed with central silver/white flattened crown; folded leaf buds, 1-mm notched membrane, coarse two-ranked zipperlike spikelets in digitate head.

Digitaria ciliaris / crabgrasses — seedheads can radiate too, but many species have blades ROLLED in the bud and paired rather than multi-flowered dense Eleusine spikelets; base generally less silvery and less compressed.
Cynodon dactylon — rooted creeping aboveground stolons and underground rhizomes; collar ligule is a HAIR FRINGE, not an entire short notched membrane; flower branches often more slender.
Chloris virgata — fingerlike inflorescences but the individual spikelets show conspicuous long awns and hairy/feathery appearance, unlike goosegrass's comparatively neat awnless rows.
Dactyloctenium aegyptium — another introduced crowfoot grass, with short broad branches that are often bristle-tipped and glumes with awns; separate from goosegrass under 10×.
comparison_lesson.caution: A fingerlike flowering head by itself cannot establish goosegrass. Check the actual plant base, collar, and mature spikelets. Range-status labels untouched.

what_to_teach_crew: Before flowering, the SILVERY COMPRESSED CROWN often reveals goosegrass in compacted turf; check leaf folding next.
Don't mistake collar hairs for the ligule: the true ligule is a short notched membrane.
A flowering head shaped like a hand can be Digitaria, Cynodon, Chloris or Eleusine. Photograph and inspect a SINGLE SPIKELET on the branch.
No systemic perennial runner network is typical for goosegrass; runners rooting at successive nodes point toward a different species.
This is an introduced turf weed, not a native restoration seed species.
The current archived photo only proves a radiating flowering head and crowding of spikelets, NOT the crown or ligule.
